parts:
Hi Deo,

I recall this result too. It’s a while since I looked but I believe what you are seeing is a result for each allele - so you get two for each locus. I recall they are identical, so you just filter one out (E.g in excel if you’re using that). I’m not sure why this result is provided, but it’s not what I expected either, so maybe a minor tweak to the coding is required Arthur & Bernd?
Cheers,
Olly

Yes that is what is happening, so basically you get one for each allele. So just use every second one for the loci. I will change that in the next iteration of dartR.

 

Cheers, Bernd

From: da...@googlegroups.com <da...@googlegroups.com> On Behalf Of Berry, Olly (NCMI, IOMRC Crawley)
Sent: Friday, 17 July 2020 10:41 AM
To: da...@googlegroups.com
Subject: Re: [dartR] Re: gl.outflank error

 

Hi Deo,

 

I recall this result too. It’s a while since I looked but I believe what you are seeing is a result for each allele - so you get two for each locus. I recall they are identical, so you just filter one out (E.g in excel if you’re using that). I’m not sure why this result is provided, but it’s not what I expected either, so maybe a minor tweak to the coding is required Arthur & Bernd?

Cheers,

Olly
